sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I would have done much better.
I might have passed with more effort.

options.text: I will pass the exam tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: This is a future plan, not an unreal past result of a missed opportunity.

options.text: I passed the exam last week.
options.why_wrong: This states a real past fact, while the stem expresses an unreal past situation that did not happen.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.
I should pass the exam now.
options.why_wrong: This uses a present obligation and does not complete the past regret introduced by 'if only'.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'if only' to express unreal past regret
explanation: The third conditional expresses an imagined past situation and its imagined result. 'If only' adds a sense of regret, so the main clause must use 'would have' followed by the past participle. Ukrainian speakers often use a simple conditional form here, but English requires the perfect infinitive to show the result is also in the past.
translation: Якби я лише краще вчився, я б склав іспит.
